acceptance: A scheduled refresh run ends failed with a message naming the still-open earlier refresh pull request of the same kind.
The jobs open and close the same pull requests as before; nothing else about the gate or the workflow's commits changed.
context: Filed 2026-11-20 from the adversarial review of the scale-factor and TPC-DI remediation work (PRs #4298-#4385 and benchbox-site #178-#210).
description:
## Problem
Scheduled baseline refresh pull requests go unattended. Fast-tier #3928, #4066 and #4283 were opened by the Monday schedule and closed unmerged days later: #4066 and #4283 were marked too large to review and waited for a stand-in; #3928 passed review and was never armed. Medium-shard #4284 (opened 2026-11-16, SHIP verdict, never armed) came to conflict with develop and was closed on 2026-11-20T14:49Z by another session or the owner, not by this work. Both kinds come from .github/workflows/fast-duration-baseline-refresh.yml (jobs `refresh` and `medium`).

## Owner decision
Chosen option: "leave the identity alone. Add only a visible failure when a scheduled refresh opens while the previous one is still open." Source: owner's answer in the choice dialog, 2026-11-20. The earlier scope of this item (a `reproduce` check, a staleness warning, a refresh cadence) was not chosen and is removed; nothing replaces it.

## Change
Read the workflow on current develop first, including what each job already does with earlier pull requests (the `medium` job closes earlier `chore/medium-durations-*` pull requests after opening a new one). Add only this: when a scheduled run finds an earlier refresh pull request of its own kind still open, the run ends as failed with a message naming that pull request and saying it was never armed or needs a stand-in. Do not change whether a pull request is opened or closed.

## Decision gates
No change to the gate, the baseline, the thresholds, the commit identity, which pull requests the jobs open or close, `.github/soundness-paths.txt` or `.github/inert-paths.txt`. If a visible failure cannot be added without changing open-or-close behaviour, stop and show the owner the choice.

## Verification rubric
Pass: workflow lint passes; a test of the new step with a fixture list of open pull requests shows the run fails and names the open one, and passes when none is open; the diff shows the open and close steps unchanged; the workflow's existing tests pass.

## Guardrails (owner, 2026-11-20)
Accepted by the owner in the choice dialog: the agent never posts a stand-in review, closes and reopens a pull request to restart CI, uses `--no-verify`, force-pushes, rewrites an author, or deletes anything under `~/Developer/benchmark_runs`. It arms with `make pr-arm` once per pull request and reports the result. Subagents are read-only. Any limit, default, threshold or label text is shown to the owner before it is committed. A blocked step stops this item; the agent moves to the next item and does not work around the block.
Review threads: the accepted text also said the agent never resolves a thread. Asked afterwards which rule applies, the owner chose: "The morning rule: I may resolve a thread once the bot has reviewed the new head and did not raise the finding again." ('I' is the agent.) So the agent pushes the fix and replies, and resolves a thread only after the bot's review of the new head does not raise that finding again.
